tests.transcriptText: Good morning, doctor. I brought my dog Usvin today because he has not been feeling well for the past three days. He is a three-year-old Labrador, and his weight is approximately 18 kg. Normally, he is very active, playful, and eats his food regularly. However, for the last three days, he has been vomiting frequently and has completely lost interest in food. Initially, I thought it was a minor stomach problem, but yesterday he vomited around four times. The vomit was mostly yellowish liquid, sometimes with a little foam. He is also drinking less water than usual. I noticed that he had loose stools twice yesterday, and today morning his stool was also watery. He seems very tired and spends most of his time lying down. One more thing I noticed is that he ate some leftover chicken from our dinner three days ago. I am not sure whether the food was fresh. Since then, his health seems to have become worse. He has not received any new medication recently His routine vaccinations are up to date and his last doorming was approximately three months ago Doctor could you please examine Ushvin and tell me what might be causing these symptoms I am particularly worried because he is not eating and is becoming weaker I understand, doctor. You mentioned that his temperature is slightly elevated and that he may be dehydrated. Is this possibly gastroenteritis, a bacterial infection, or food poisoning? Could there also be a problem with his liver or kidneys? If we need to investigate further, I would like to understand which laboratory tests are necessary. Should we perform a complete blood count to check his white blood cells, red blood cells, hemoglobin, and platelet count? Will this help identify infection or inflammation? What about the biochemical tests? I heard that kidney and liver function can be evaluated through blood biomarkers. Should we check ALT, AST, ALP, total bilirubin, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, and albumin? I would also like to know whether electrolytes such as sodium potassium and chloride should be checked because he has been vomiting and experiencing diarrhea Could dehydration of Should we also perform a blood glucose test to check his sugar level And is a Cereactive protein test useful for evaluating inflammation in his body If the blood reports are not sufficient, do you recommend a stool examination or abdominal ultrasound? I want to make sure we do not miss any serious underlying condition, especially an intestinal obstruction or another abdominal problem. Okay, Doctor. Please proceed with the recommended investigations. Now that the preliminary examination is complete, could you explain the treatment plan? Since Ashwin is dehydrated, will he require intravenous fluid therapy? What type of fluids would be appropriate based on his electrolyte levels and hydration status? What medication would you recommend for controlling his vomiting? Is an antiemetic such as Maropitin appropriate in his case? If the patient is on a diet he should we give him probiotics to support his digestive system And if there is evidence of a bacterial infection would antibiotics be necessary or should we wait for the test results before deciding Doctor, could you please explain the medication dosage, frequency, duration, and whether each medicine should be given before or after food? I want to make sure I administer everything correctly. Also, what kind of diet should I provide once his vomiting is controlled? Can I give him a veterinary gastrointestinal diet in small portions? How much water should he drink during recovery? One final question, Doctor. How long will it normally take for him to recover? Should we repeat the CBC, kidney function, liver function, and electrolyte tests after a few days to monitor his improvement? I will follow all the instructions and bring him back for the recommended follow-up examination. Please let me know immediately if any of the laboratory results indicate something serious. Thank you so much, doctor. I hope Ashvin recovers quickly.

tests.transcriptText: Good morning, doctor. I brought my dog Bruno because he has not been feeling well for the past two days. He has been vomiting frequently and is not eating properly. Yesterday, he vomited around three times, and today morning, he vomited twice. Sometimes the vomit looks like a yellow liquid. He is also drinking very little water compared to usual. He had loose motion twice yesterday, and his stool is still not normal today. Yesterday evening, he ate some leftover chicken from our dinner. I'm not sure whether it was fresh. Normally, Bruno is very active and likes running around the house, but since yesterday, he has been very tired and mostly lying on the floor. Doctor, is this something serious? He has received all his regular vaccinations, and his last vaccination was around six months ago. Okay, doctor. Please examine him and let me know what the problem could be. I understand. Do you think it could be a stomach infection or something related to the food he ate? What tests do you recommend to identify the exact problem? Will he need a blood test or any other laboratory investigation? Doctor, what about medication? Does he need any treatment to stop the vomiting? Should I give him food and water normally at home, or should I follow any special diet? Okay, doctor. I will follow your instructions. Please let me know when we should come back for a follow-up consultation. Thank you, doctor. I hope Bruno feels better soon.

clinical_extraction.clinical_summary: Ashwin presented for veterinary evaluation with chief concerns: Coughing, Lethargy, Mild anorexia. Reported symptoms: Decreased appetite. Patient assessed by Dr Mouni for clinical monitoring.

transcript_evidence.quote: Refusing dry kibble, only having small amounts of wet food
transcript_evidence.speaker: owner

medical_history.vaccination_status: Up to date with core vaccines, Bordetella due

observations.finding: Bilateral mild tracheal sensitivity on palpation, no audible crackles

transcript_evidence.quote: Lungs sound clear, but there is mild tracheal sensitivity
transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

observations.finding: Normal heart rate and rhythm, strong femoral pulses

transcript_evidence.quote: Heart sounds good, normal rhythm
transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

diagnoses.clinical_reasoning: Acute onset of paroxysmal cough following dog park exposure, tracheal sensitivity

transcript_evidence.quote: This looks like mild kennel cough or infectious tracheobronchitis
transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

medications.special_instructions: Give with food or treat to avoid esophageal irritation
medications.doctor_notes: Antibiotic therapy for secondary bacterial tracheobronchitis

transcript_evidence.quote: We will prescribe Doxycycline 100mg, one tablet twice daily with food for 10 days
transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

medications.frequency: Every 8 to 12 hours as needed for coughing
medications.special_instructions: May cause mild sedation; give when coughing prevents resting

transcript_evidence.quote: For the cough relief, half a tablet of cough suppressant twice a day as needed
transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

lab_tests.clinical_reason: Rule out pneumonia if fever or respiratory distress develops
lab_tests.instructions: Recommended if coughing persists past day 7 or worsens

transcript_evidence.quote: If she does not improve in a few days we should take chest X-rays
transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

transcript_evidence.quote: We could do a respiratory swab panel if needed
transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

follow_up.reason: Re-evaluation of coughing and tracheal sensitivity
monitoring_instructions: Monitor daily respiratory rate at rest (normal is under 30 breaths/min)
Ensure pet consumes fresh water and keeps hydrated
Avoid leash collar pressure on neck; switch to harness during walks
warning_signs: Labored breathing, wheezing, or panting while resting
Lethargy worsening or total refusal to eat and drink
Cough producing thick yellow/green discharge or blood

transcript_evidence.quote: Bring Bella back in one week if coughing continues or immediately if breathing is heavy
transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

missing_info: Confirmed Bordetella vaccine date from previous veterinary clinic record

content.title: Veterinary Prescription — Ashwin
content.dispense_instructions: Dispense exact quantity as formulated. Label with pet name and instructions.

evidence.quote: Should we perform a complete blood count to check his white blood cells, red blood cells, hemoglobin, and platelet count?
evidence.speaker: doctor

A.clinical_notes: Consistent presentation with acute clinical onset.

content.overview: Patient Ashwin, a 3‑year‑old golden retriever, presented for a routine check‑up. Auscultation revealed clear lungs bilaterally and a heart rate of 110 beats per minute. No abnormalities were noted during the examination.

transcript_evidence.speaker: doctor

content.owner_guidance: Re-check recommended in None. Monitor appetite, hydration, and activity levels closely at home.
